  • I am a family of one. I have a debt of 100 dollars, X amount of which is due next month (assume a 0% interest rate so that X is not important; this is a fair assumption since interest rates are currently extremely low).

  • I have an income of 200 dollars.
  • For the past four months I have spent 100 dollars on rent and 125 dollars on hookers and blow, every month.

I can (a) raise my debt ceiling to 125 USD and continue to spend money I don't have or (b) decrease my hookers and blow expenditure to 100 dollars or less and either roll over X amount of debt or, if I decrease my hookers and blow expenditure to less than 100 dollars, roll over X - Y amount of debt, where Y is the amount of debt I pay back with the leftovers from my former hookers and blow budget.

In the real world you have to decrease spending by a little more to account for debt interest, but the same fundamental logic applies: if you reduce your spending enough you don't need to go into further debt. This is not rocket science.
